title: Rocks and Minerals
summary: Identify rocks and minerals from observable evidence, explain how rocks form, and make defensible decisions under station timing.
objectives: Distinguish observations from inferences and select diagnostic tests.
Identify minerals using physical properties and an evidence-first workflow.
Classify igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks from texture and formation evidence.
Document an identification so another competitor can follow the reasoning.

units.title: Observe Like a Geologist
units.summary: Build the evidence habits that make every later identification more reliable.
objectives: Separate a rock, mineral, and manufactured material.
Record observations before naming a specimen.

lessons.title: Rocks, Minerals, and Evidence
lessons.objective: Distinguish a mineral from a rock and justify the distinction with observable or structural evidence.

lessons.title: Observe Before You Identify
lessons.objective: Separate observation from inference and record a repeatable evidence profile.

units.title: Mineral Properties
units.summary: Use diagnostic physical properties instead of relying on color or first impressions.
objectives: Perform common property tests safely.
Choose the next test that best separates remaining candidates.

lessons.title: Color, Streak, and Luster
lessons.objective: Compare surface color, powdered streak, and luster and explain which observations are most diagnostic.

lessons.title: Hardness and the Mohs Scale
lessons.objective: Bracket an unknown mineral's hardness with scratch tests and state the result without overclaiming.

lessons.title: Cleavage, Fracture, Density and Magnetism
lessons.objective: Describe cleavage by the NUMBER of directions and the ANGLES between them — mica one, orthoclase two at 90 degrees, plagioclase two at about 86 degrees with striations, halite and galena three at 90 degrees, calcite three not at 90 degrees, fluorite four — distinguish it from conchoidal and uneven fracture, compare specific gravity by heft, and use magnetite as the strongly magnetic mineral. Never describe cleavage with Miller indices, which a student cannot observe.

units.title: The Rock Cycle
units.summary: Explain rock change as a set of processes rather than a single circular path.
objectives: Connect processes to rock-type changes.
Interpret more than one valid path through the rock cycle.

lessons.title: Processes That Change Rock
lessons.objective: Connect melting, cooling, weathering, erosion, deposition, lithification, heat, and pressure to rock change.

lessons.title: Reason Through Rock-Cycle Paths
lessons.objective: Trace and defend multiple possible transformations between rock types.

units.title: Igneous Rocks
units.summary: Read cooling history from texture and connect mineral composition to classification.
objectives: Infer cooling conditions from texture.
Classify common igneous specimens with texture and composition together.

lessons.title: Cooling History and Igneous Texture
lessons.objective: Infer intrusive or extrusive cooling history from crystal size and texture.

lessons.title: Composition and Bowen's Reaction Series
lessons.objective: Use mineral composition and Bowen's reaction series as supporting evidence in igneous classification.

units.title: Sedimentary and Metamorphic Rocks
units.summary: Connect texture and structures to the processes that produced a rock.
objectives: Classify sedimentary rocks by material and texture.
Use foliation, grain change, and composition to classify metamorphic rocks.

lessons.title: Sedimentary Evidence
lessons.objective: Classify clastic, chemical, and biochemical sedimentary rocks from grains, structures, and composition.

lessons.title: Metamorphic Evidence
lessons.objective: Distinguish foliated and nonfoliated metamorphic rocks and connect texture to heat, pressure, and parent material.

units.title: The Mohs Scale and the Tools You Are Handed
units.summary: The ten index minerals in order, and the hardness of the copper cube, glass plate and streak plate a station gives you.
objectives: Recite the Mohs scale in order
Convert a scratch result into a hardness number

lessons.title: The Ten Index Minerals, in Order
lessons.objective: State the Mohs scale in order — talc, gypsum, calcite, fluorite, apatite, orthoclase, quartz, topaz, corundum, diamond — and explain why it is ordinal rather than linear.

lessons.title: Fingernail, Copper, Glass and Streak Plate
lessons.objective: Give the approximate hardness of a fingernail, a copper coin, a glass plate or steel nail and a streak plate, and use them to bracket an unknown's hardness.

units.title: Mineral Families: How the National List Is Organised
units.summary: The List groups its minerals by chemical family. Knowing the family narrows an unknown before any test.
objectives: Name the family of any mineral on the List
Recognise the diagnostic property of each family

lessons.title: Carbonates and Borates
lessons.objective: Identify calcite, dolomite, aragonite, azurite, malachite, magnesite, rhodochrosite, siderite and ulexite, and state the acid test that marks a carbonate.

lessons.title: Native Elements and Oxides
lessons.objective: Identify silver, copper, sulfur, graphite, diamond, corundum, hematite, magnetite, goethite, rutile and zincite, and say what each family's members have in common. Also gold and pyrolusite.

lessons.title: Sulfides, Sulfates and Phosphates
lessons.objective: Identify galena, pyrite, chalcopyrite, bornite, sphalerite and stibnite; gypsum, alabaster, barite and celestite; and apatite, pyromorphite, vanadinite and turquoise. Also the halides halite and fluorite; the three gypsum varieties selenite (crystalline), satin spar (fibrous) and alabaster (massive); and fluorapatite within the apatite group.

lessons.title: Feldspars, Pyroxenes and Amphiboles
lessons.objective: Distinguish plagioclase from potassium feldspar by cleavage angle and striations, and identify albite, amazonite, orthoclase, microcline, augite, actinolite and tremolite. Name the feldspar, pyroxene and amphibole GROUPS as the List does, and include labradorite (with its play of colour), hornblende, and sodalite.

lessons.title: Micas, Clays, Talc, Beryl and Tourmaline
lessons.objective: Identify muscovite, biotite, lepidolite, kaolinite, talc, beryl, tourmaline, chrysocolla, apophyllite, prehnite and stilbite by habit, cleavage and hardness. Name the mica group as the List does, and add dioptase and rhodonite.

lessons.title: Garnets, Olivine, Topaz and the Metamorphic Silicates
lessons.objective: Identify the garnet group (almandine, grossular), olivine, topaz, kyanite, staurolite, epidote, willemite, wollastonite and spodumene. Also zircon, and name the garnet GROUP as the List does.

units.title: Quartz Varieties, Gemstones and Organic Gems
units.summary: Competition directions require the complete name including variety. These are the specimens where the variety IS the answer.
objectives: Name every quartz variety on the List from colour and habit
Explain why pearl and amber are not minerals

lessons.title: Quartz and Its Varieties
lessons.objective: Identify rock crystal, milky, rose, smoky, amethyst and citrine quartz, and the microcrystalline varieties agate, chalcedony, jasper, aventurine and tiger's eye, plus opal as a mineraloid.

lessons.title: Gem Varieties: Emerald, Ruby, Sapphire and the Rest
lessons.objective: Name the mineral behind each gem variety on the List: emerald, aquamarine and morganite (beryl); ruby and sapphire (corundum); kunzite and hiddenite (spodumene); peridot (olivine).

lessons.title: Pearl and Amber: Why They Are Not Minerals
lessons.objective: Apply the five-part definition of a mineral to pearl and amber and explain which criterion each fails, and why opal is a mineraloid.

units.title: Naming the Rocks on the List
units.summary: Identification is 30-50% of the score and the List names 47 rocks. Each one here is named, placed in its class, and tied to the evidence that identifies it.
objectives: Name any igneous rock from composition and texture
Name any sedimentary rock from grain size or origin

lessons.title: The Igneous Rocks: Composition by Texture
lessons.objective: Place granite, rhyolite, diorite, andesite, gabbro, basalt, peridotite, syenite and pegmatite in the composition-by-texture grid, and identify obsidian, pumice, scoria and tuff breccia from texture alone.

lessons.title: Clastic Rocks by Grain Size
lessons.objective: Name shale, siltstone, sandstone, arkose, greywacke, conglomerate and breccia from grain size, sorting, roundness and composition. Distinguish quartz sandstone from arkose and greywacke by composition.

lessons.title: Chemical and Biochemical Rocks
lessons.objective: Identify rock salt, rock gypsum, travertine, chert and flint, dolostone, chalk, fossil limestone, coquina, bauxite and banded iron formation, and say which are chemical and which biochemical. Also diatomite and oolitic limestone.

lessons.title: Coal: Lignite to Anthracite
lessons.objective: Order peat, lignite, bituminous coal and anthracite by rank and carbon content, and explain what burial, heat and time do at each step.

lessons.title: Metamorphic Rocks and Their Parent Rocks
lessons.objective: Name slate, phyllite, schist, garnet schist, gneiss, marble, quartzite, serpentinite, soapstone and amphibolite, and give each one's protolith. Include mica schist alongside garnet schist.

lessons.title: Metamorphic Grade, Index Minerals, Contact and Regional
lessons.objective: Order chlorite, muscovite, biotite, garnet, staurolite, kyanite and sillimanite by metamorphic grade, and distinguish contact from regional metamorphism.

units.title: Identification and Competition
units.summary: Turn property knowledge into an efficient, documented station workflow.
objectives: Navigate a mineral flowchart without guessing.
Use an elimination workflow under time pressure.
Write evidence-based station answers.

lessons.title: Use an Identification Flowchart
lessons.objective: Navigate a mineral flowchart by making and verifying one evidence-based split at a time.

lessons.title: Identify an Unknown Specimen
lessons.objective: Choose an efficient sequence of tests, eliminate alternatives, and state a defensible identification.

lessons.title: Station Strategy and Documentation
lessons.objective: Allocate station time, record evidence compactly, and recover when an initial hypothesis fails.
